note: Draft 1's lines for the story gate's timed read. n.. = the narrator (af_heart, task 'takes'); s01 the stall-keeper, c01/c02 the constable, t01 the tea man, auditioned across the cast (task 'cast'). 'constable' planned as KUN-stuh-bul (the Indian and British stress) for af_heart.
ref_text: The market opens slowly in the mornings. Shutters rattle up one by one, a radio plays somewhere behind a wall, and the first customers stand at the counter counting out their change.

lines.text: You'll only hear what was in that box once, so remember every word.
Whatever the constable writes down is what the police will go looking for.
lines.text_kokoro: Whatever the [constable](/kˈʌnstəbəl/) writes down is what the police will go looking for.

lines.text: My box! Milk, sugar, ginger, cardamom, the cups, the strainer, the biscuits, my kettle, the spoons!
The kettle, the spoons, and the tea.
So the report said tea, and the constable went looking for it.
lines.text_kokoro: So the report said tea, and the [constable](/kˈʌnstəbəl/) went looking for it.

lines.text: He brings her tea every morning, which is why there was never any tea in the box, and why there won't be any today.
Every word she said made you think of tea, so your memory kept the tea and let the words go.
If you said no, name the nine things she did say.
